title: Recent personal art-making is age-patterned while perceived local cultural opportunity is income-patterned
source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau Household Trends and Outlook Pulse Survey, July 2026 topical tables 2607; arts production and local opportunity tables
geography: United States; adults age 18 and older living in housing units

observations.period: July 15-August 3, 2026; personal art creation, practice, or performance during the prior four weeks

denominator.unit: estimated U.S. civilian population age 18 and older in the published weighted-count table; total row

personal_art_total.unit: percent creating, practicing, or performing personal art in the last four weeks, calculated among reported responses

personal_art_age_18_34.unit: percent among adults ages 18-34, calculated among reported responses

personal_art_age_65_plus.unit: percent among adults age 65 and older, calculated among reported responses

age_gradient.unit: percentage-point gap between ages 18-34 and 65+, calculated from published weighted counts

mechanism.value: Personal cultural production is not distributed like recent attendance alone: the four-week practice/creation measure is higher among younger adults, leaving an open route through time, life stage, work, care, venue, digital tools, and informal cultural production

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Census HTOPS July 2026 Arts Table 2. Percentages are calculated from published weighted counts, excluding the did-not-report category from each denominator.
observations.uncertainty: HTOPS is an experimental cross-sectional product. Personal art includes creation, practice, or performance in a four-week recall window; the age difference is descriptive and does not identify causal effects of age, time, work, care, health, technology, or cultural preference.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults age 18 and older by age group.
observations.counterinterpretation: The result may reflect life stage, available time, survey interpretation, health, household composition, or different forms of cultural practice; it is not a measure of artistic quality, professional creative work, or total annual participation.

observations.period: July 15-August 3, 2026; perceived neighborhood or community arts and cultural opportunities

denominator.unit: estimated U.S. civilian population age 18 and older in the published weighted-count table; total row

plenty_local_arts_opportunities_total.unit: percent agreeing or strongly agreeing that there are plenty of opportunities to take part in arts and cultural activities locally, calculated among reported responses

plenty_local_arts_opportunities_under_35.unit: percent among adults in households with income below $35,000, calculated among reported responses

plenty_local_arts_opportunities_150000_p.unit: percent among adults in households with income of $150,000 or more, calculated among reported responses

income_gradient.unit: percentage-point gap between the highest and lowest published household-income groups

mechanism.value: Local cultural supply is experienced through unequal conversion capacity: the income gradient may reflect geography, transport, price, time, information, safety, disability access, household resources, or differences in expectations and recognition of what counts as an opportunity

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Census HTOPS July 2026 Arts Table 3. The positive share combines strongly agree and agree; percentages are calculated from published weighted counts after excluding did-not-report responses.
observations.uncertainty: This is perceived local opportunity, not a venue census, attendance measure, or objective supply estimate. The income gradient is cross-sectional and cannot identify whether price, transport, supply, information, safety, accessibility, preference, or selection explains the difference.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults age 18 and older by household-income category.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher-income respondents may live in places with different cultural supply or may define opportunities differently; lower reported opportunity does not prove cultural absence, and local opportunity does not establish affordability, welcome, or actual participation.

HTOPS July 2026 sample design, 12,755 respondents, weighting, cross-sectional design, response rates, and experimental-data caveats.

boundary: This record adds a same-instrument descriptive bridge between cultural production, perceived local cultural supply, age, and household income. It uses experimental cross-sectional HTOPS weighted counts and does not establish causal age or income effects, objective venue supply, affordability, cultural quality, belonging, or longitudinal change.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Census HTOPS July 2026 table index, source-and-accuracy statement, Arts Table 2, and Arts Table 3 retrieved; weighted total rows, age and income rows, category definitions, and missing-report treatment reviewed.
